subject: Architecture
title: Suspension Bridges: Hanging by Cables
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Suspension Bridges: Hanging by Cables.

hook.text: Suspension bridges hang from cables — the deck literally floats between towers on strands of steel wire.

buildup.text: Main cables drape between tall towers. Vertical suspender cables connect the main cables to the deck below.

discovery.text: Each main cable contains thousands of individual wires — bundled together, they can support enormous loads.

twist.text: Suspension bridges are flexible by design. In strong wind, the deck sways several feet side to side.

climax.text: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in Japan has the world's longest span — 6,532 feet of suspended roadway.

punchline.text: Steel wires thinner than pencils hold up a mile of highway.

quiz.question: What is the world's longest suspension bridge span?
options: The Golden Gate Bridge at 4,200 feet
The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge at 6,532 feet
